cut.v-arpege: Duplicate record of L'Arpège (v-l-arpege), without coordinates: merged.
cut.v-le-cinq-four-seasons-george-v: Duplicate record of Le Cinq, without coordinates: merged into the cut below.
cut.v-le-cinq: Cap: the three-star lane keeps L'Arpège (the vegetable revolution), Plénitude (the sauce house on the Seine) and Kei (the Japanese-born chef who took three French stars). Le Cinq is a fine palace room that teaches the least about Paris itself.
cut.v-epicure-le-bristol: Cap: a fourth palace three-star; the grand-hotel register is told by Plénitude and, for a drink, by Le Bar du Bristol under Boire & sortir.
cut.v-pierre-gagnaire: Cap: a fifth three-star; the lane holds three that each say something different, and the old record carried no coordinates or story of its own.
cut.v-le-chateaubriand: Cut: its own old record says 'winding down', it had no coordinates, and the neo-bistro story it started is told by Septime, Le Servan and Clown Bar.
cut.v-allard: Bistro cap: Paul Bert, Chez L'Ami Jean and Chez Georges tell the canon; Allard's 1932 Left Bank room is the one cut a duck-with-olives lover may regret.
